result.topic_en: Draft notes on the general expression of a function on the surface T that becomes infinite of the first order at given points, written as a linear combination of elementary integrals with constant coefficients, on fixing those constants so that the periodicity moduli vanish, and on the rule that integrals around points of infinity of higher order are zero.

methods.what: General form of a function on the surface T with simple poles at given points: linear combination of elementary integrals t, integrals of the first kind w, and a constant
methods.quote: $s = \beta_1 t_1 + \beta_2 t_2 + \cdots + \beta_\mu t_\mu + \alpha_1 w_1 + \alpha_2 w_2 + \cdots \alpha_p w_p + \mathrm{const.}$

methods.what: The periodicity moduli are linear in the constants, so they can all be made to vanish once the number of poles is at least p+1
methods.quote:
Wenn $\mu \geqq p + 1$ ist, {+also+} lassen sich die Größen $\alpha$ und
$\beta$ so bestimmen, daß die Periodicitätsmoduln sämmtlich = 0 werden.

methods.what: Argument principle: the integral of d log(s-a) over the boundary vanishes, so the function takes every value as often as it has poles
methods.quote:
Eine solche Function, die $m$ mal unendlich und auch [?] ... Linie unstetig wird, nimmt jeden
[-Werth-] {+Werth+} $m$ mal an.
